title: AuthZ/Audit/KMS onboarding: exit criteria, rollback and scope-deltas
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket captures the product requirements and acceptance criteria for onboarding customer tenants into Private deployments with enterprise-grade Identity and Key management. Scope covers SSO/SAML IdP integrations, RBAC role mappings, audit-log schema and retention, and KMS/HSM integration patterns. The deliverable is a verified, signoff-ready checklist and test runbook to hand off to the Onboarding & SRE teams.
decision_log: 2026-02-12: Agreed with Security that minimum audit retention for enterprise customers is 365 days (Aisha P.).
2026-02-19: Chosen IdP metadata exchange flow is SP-initiated SAML with optional OIDC support for modern partners (Marcus N.).
2026-02-26: KMS plan: default integration via customer KMS credentials; offer HSM-backed key wrap as a paid option (Security review).
2026-03-05: RBAC model standardized to role templates (Admin, Operator, Auditor, Viewer) with tenant scoping; decision to implement attribute-based assertions for non-standard roles.
acceptance_criteria: SSO/SAML: Customer IdP metadata uploaded and validated; SP-initiated login tested across two IdP vendors and documented.
RBAC: Role templates deployed and verify that role assignment enforces access boundaries for console and API (no privilege escalation in tests).
Audit logs: Events emitted for authz decisions, key usage, config changes, and model-serving access; logs written to configured customer sink and retained for configured retention period.
KMS/HSM: Customer-managed keys can be registered and used for envelope encryption; key rotation validated with zero-data-loss test and 2 recovery scenarios.
Signoff: Security, Product, Onboarding, and Legal provide written signoff and attach evidence artifacts (test runbook, audit sample, IdP logs, PRs).
checklist: IdP metadata exchange documented and sample metadata stored in Confluence page.
SAML response validation unit and integration tests merged (PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4892).
RBAC templates checked into configuration repo and feature-flagged for canary tenants.
Audit schema documented and mapping to customer SIEM provided (JSON schema link in Confluence).
KMS integration tested with AWS KMS and Vault HSM; test vectors attached.
Operational runbook includes alert thresholds for excessive 'deny' rates and key-access anomalies.
Rollback procedures for onboarding step failures are drafted and validated in staging with test tenant.
Privacy checklist (PII-free audit payloads) reviewed by Legal and accepted.
test_plan: Identity: SP-initiated SAML login test matrix across Okta and Azure AD, including attribute mapping variations.
RBAC: Attempt privilege escalation from Viewer role; confirm denied and audit event emitted.
Audit: Inject synthetic events and verify delivery to S3 and Splunk sinks, retention and exportability.
KMS: Rotate an active CMK and run multi-region decryption checks; simulate key compromise and recovery flow.
End-to-end: Onboard a pilot customer in staging and run a 48-hour traffic soak with monitoring for failed auth, token expiry, and key errors.
signoff: Product (Aisha Patel) - approves acceptance criteria and rollout plan.
Security (Jordan Lee) - approves KMS/HSM choices and audit retention policy after review.
Onboarding (Rina Gomez) - verifies runbook and rollback steps are operationally feasible.
Legal (Marco Silva) - approves data-handling and export controls for audit artifacts.
SRE (Marcus Nguyen) - confirms deployment automation, alerts, and runbooks are complete.

2026-03-02: Onboarding runbook draft reviewed by Rina G.; added explicit rollback step for partially-provisioned keys.

risks: Customers using legacy IdP flows may require additional engineering work (timeboxing recommended).
HSM integration increases support overhead and may delay onboarding for certain customers.
Audit retention requirements across regions could conflict with customer data residency constraints.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Feature-flag RBAC and SAML metadata upload for internal canary tenants (2 tenants).
Phase 2: Invite 3 pilot customers with differing IdP vendors; validate end-to-end and collect artifacts.
Phase 3: Open rollout to Early Access customers; monitor key-access metrics and audit delivery for 14 days.
Phase 4: General availability after signoff and legal acceptance.
